name: Northern Cardinal
fact: During courtship the male feeds seeds to the female beak to beak. Males are so territorial they will fight their own reflection in windows and car mirrors, sometimes for days.
question: Why does a cardinal keep pecking at your window?
answer: It thinks its reflection is a rival male invading its territory.

name: Arctic Tern
fact: Arctic Terns fly from the Arctic to Antarctica and back every year. Birds tracked from Greenland and Iceland averaged about 70,900 km (44,000 miles) a year, and because they chase summer at both poles they see two summers every year.
question: About how far does an Arctic Tern fly in a year?
answer: Around 70,900 km (44,000 miles) on average, the longest migration known of any animal.

name: Ruby-throated Hummingbird
fact: A hummingbird's heart can beat up to 1,260 times a minute. Even so, some Ruby-throats cross the Gulf of Mexico nonstop on migration, with nowhere to land and nothing to eat along the way.
question: Guess: how many times a minute can its heart beat?
answer: Up to about 1,260. Yours beats about 60 to 100.

name: Peregrine Falcon
fact: When it dives on prey (a move called a stoop), the Peregrine Falcon is the fastest animal on Earth. One falcon was clocked at 389 km/h (242 mph) in a 2005 dive.
question: Fastest animal alive: cheetah or Peregrine Falcon?
answer: The Peregrine Falcon, in a dive. A cheetah tops out around 100 km/h (65 mph).

name: Common Raven
fact: Ravens are some of the smartest birds around. Like their crow cousins, they can mimic sounds from their surroundings, including human speech.
question: Can a raven learn to talk?
answer: Yes. Ravens can mimic sounds around them, including human words.

name: Atlantic Puffin
fact: That bright orange beak is a seasonal look. After breeding season puffins shed the colorful outer plates of their bills, so in winter the beak is smaller and duller, and the color grows back in spring.
question: Is a puffin's beak bright orange all year?
answer: No. The colorful bill plates are shed after breeding season and grow back in spring.

name: Great Horned Owl
fact: Great Horned Owls are one of the few animals that regularly hunt skunks. Their poor sense of smell means the spray barely bothers them.
question: What smelly animal is on this owl's menu?
answer: Skunks. The owl's weak sense of smell makes the spray no big deal.

name: Shoebill
fact: Shoebills of Africa's swamps hunt by standing almost perfectly still, then lunging at fish like lungfish. They are mostly silent, but at the nest they clatter their huge bills, and begging chicks sound a lot like a person with hiccups.
question: What do hungry shoebill chicks sound like?

name: American Crow
fact: Crows remember human faces. Researchers in Seattle banded crows while wearing masks, and later the crows scolded anyone wearing that mask, even crows that never saw the banding happen.
question: If you bother a crow, will it remember you?
answer: Yes. Crows recognize individual faces and can even teach other crows who to watch out for.

name: North Island Brown Kiwi
fact: A kiwi's egg can be up to 20% of the mother's body weight, one of the biggest eggs for its size of any bird. Kiwi are also the only birds with nostrils at the tip of the beak, which they use to sniff out worms underground.
question: Where are a kiwi's nostrils?
answer: At the very tip of its long beak, for smelling food in the soil.

name: Blue Jay
fact: Blue Jays aren't actually blue. Their feathers have no blue pigment. The color comes from the way light scatters inside the feather, and if you crush a blue feather, the blue disappears.
question: What color is a Blue Jay's feather pigment?
answer: Not blue. The pigment is melanin (brown/black). The blue is a trick of light.

name: Wandering Albatross
fact: The Wandering Albatross has the longest wingspan of any living bird, up to about 3.7 m (12 ft). Some individuals have been tracked flying around the entire Southern Ocean three times in a single year.
question: How wide can its wings get?
answer: Up to about 3.7 m (12 ft), wider than a car is long.

name: Wild Turkey
fact: Unlike farm turkeys, wild turkeys are agile, fast fliers, and they're among the heaviest flying birds in the world. At dusk they fly up into trees to roost for the night, safe from predators.
question: Can wild turkeys fly?
answer: Yes, and fast. They even sleep up in trees.

name: Greater Roadrunner
fact: Roadrunners can fly a little, but they prefer to run, at up to about 32 km/h (20 mph). They're quick enough to catch lizards, scorpions, and even young rattlesnakes.
question: Fly or run: which does a roadrunner prefer?
answer: Run. It can hit about 20 mph and spends most of its time on the ground.
